fact: ITWeb reports, citing Standard Bank, that CIPS interbank payments between Africa and China in renminbi have gone live and were inaugurated at the South African Reserve Bank.
Standard Bank says China's CIPS has gone live for interbank payments between Africa and China in renminbi, inaugurated at the South African Reserve Bank in November 2025.
Standard Bank says it was granted a licence at the Lujiazui Forum to offer CIPS transactions for renminbi interbank payments between Africa and China, available on its platforms from September 2025.
The document says Transactions Cleared on an Immediate Basis (TCIB) is being developed to enable immediate low-value cross-border payments in the region.
Standard Bank's Nthabiseng Sibanda says the bank uses China's CIPS as a direct route for renminbi transactions, reaching 12 African countries.
Standard Bank's Nthabiseng Sibanda says the bank has processed more than R21 billion ($1.3 billion) through CIPS since its inception.
Notice 2024 of 2022 records the SARB designating the SADC Real Time Gross Settlement System (SADC-RTGS) as a designated settlement system in place of SIRESS.

The SARB speech says lower-value retail regional payments run through SADC-RTGS now, with qualifying payments under R100,000 to move to TCIB by end-April 2027 and a hub-and-spoke pilot across eight countries by October 2027.

The South African Reserve Bank says on 23 June 2026 that its payment system and financial surveillance departments are drafting rules for cross-border payment facilitators, with a draft FinSurv circular issued in December 2025 on cross-border settlement and reporting.

fact: The South African Reserve Bank Financial Surveillance Department issued for consultation a draft exchange control circular letting payment aggregators partner Authorised Dealers to process cross-border retail e-commerce payments by residents, up to R50 000 per transaction, after two regulatory sandbox use cases.

MTN South Africa's MoMo app launched 25 additional wallet corridors, letting users in South Africa send money to wallets in Mozambique, Malawi and the Democratic Republic of Congo among others, at a 4% launch fee.
MTN South Africa said on 15 April 2024 that MoMo added 25 outbound wallet corridors from South Africa to 10 African countries, at a 4% fee with immediate clearing.

TechCentral reports that BankservAfrica, the South African clearing house behind PayShap, launched its Transactions Cleared on an Immediate Basis (TCIB) offering in February 2024 for remittance flows in the SADC region.
IT-Online reports that BankservAfrica opened the first instant low-value digital payment corridor between South Africa and Zambia on 1 March 2024, after SendHome and SamPay joined the TCIB scheme.
IT-Online reports that the SADC TCIB scheme, live since 2021 and operated by BankservAfrica, now carries the South Africa-Zambia corridor, with SendHome and SamPay as its newest participants.

The South African Reserve Bank directive says low-value cross-border electronic funds transfers within the Common Monetary Area (Eswatini, Lesotho, Namibia, South Africa) are currently executed through SADC-RTGS.

The South African Reserve Bank directive says Common Monetary Area low-value transfers, including this country's, run through the SADC-RTGS regional system and must move to the TCIB scheme by April 2027.

The CMA Cross-border Payments Oversight Committee's paper of 31 July 2024 says rand cross-border low-value EFTs within the Common Monetary Area, including South Africa, run through an interim supplementary-file solution in place since 1 October 2019 and still in use.

The CMA committee's paper of 31 July 2024 says banks route low-value cross-border EFTs within the CMA, South Africa among its four members, through the SADC real-time gross settlement system under the interim arrangement, to move to a designated retail system such as TCIB from 1 April 2027.
